title: Generation of versatile ss-dsDNA hybrid substrates for single-molecule analysis
protocol: Phosphorylate 14 nM λ DNA.
Pipette 41.6 μL of λ DNA (300 μg/mL).
Add 8.4 μL milliQ H2O to the mixture.
Add 5.6 μL 10×T4 DNA ligase buffer.
Add 0.5 μL polynucleotide kinase for a final concentration of 250 U/mL.
Pipette 3.2 μL of end-cap 1 (62 μM, PAGE-purified).
Add 14.3 μL milliQ H2O to the mixture.
Add 2 μL 10×T4 DNA ligase buffer.
Add 0.5 μL polynucleotide kinase for a final concentration of 1000 U/mL.
Pipette 2.7 μL of end-cap 2 (73 μM, PAGE-purified).
Add 14.8 μL milliQ H2O to the mixture.
Add 2 μL 10×T4 DNA ligase buffer.
Add 0.5 μL polynucleotide kinase for a final concentration of 1000 U/mL.
Mix very gently with pipette tip.
Pipette up-and-down 1–2 times using cut pipette tips.
Incubate the reactions at 37°C for 1 hour.
Mix 50 μL of 10× T4 DNA ligase buffer with the solution.
Add 400 μL of milliQ H2O to the mixture.
Pipette 56 μL of 14 nM phosphorylated λ DNA into the solution.
Add 1 μL of 10 μM phosphorylated end-cap 1 to the mixture.
Heat the mixture to 80°C for 5 minutes.
Cool the heated mixture rapidly on ice.
Add T4 DNA ligase (0.5 μL, 400 units) and incubate at 37°C for 1 hour or at 25°C for 2 hours or at 16°C for 12 hours.
Pipette 10 μL of 10 μM phosphorylated end-cap 2 into the solution.
Heat the mixture to 80°C for 5 minutes.
Cool the heated mixture rapidly on ice.
Add T4 DNA ligase enzyme (4 μL, 200 units) and incubate at 37°C for 1 hour or at 25°C for 2 hours or at 16°C for 12 hours.
Inactivate the ligase at 65°C for 20 minutes.
Pipette 2 μL of 5 μM crRNA λ2 into a new mix.
Add 1 μL of 10 μM trRNA to the crRNA λ2 mix.
Mix 4 μL of 1× T50 with the solution.
Add 1 μL of milliQ H2O to complete the crRNA λ2:tracr RNA mix preparation.
Pipette 2 μL of 5 μM crRNA λ5 into a new mix.
Add 1 μL of 10 μM trRNA to the crRNA λ5 mix.
Mix 4 μL of 1× T50 with the solution for crRNA λ5:tracr RNA.
Add 1 μL of milliQ H2O to complete the crRNA λ5:tracr RNA mix preparation.
Pipette 2 μL of 5 μM crRNA λ4 into a new mix.
Add 1 μL of 10 μM trRNA to the crRNA λ4 mix.
Mix 4 μL of 1× T50 with the solution for crRNA λ4:tracr RNA.
Add 1 μL of milliQ H2O to complete the crRNA λ4:tracr RNA mix preparation.
Pipette 2 μL of 5 μM crRNA λ4.2 into a new mix.
Add 1 μL of 10 μM trRNA to the crRNA λ4.2 mix.
Mix 4 μL of 1× T50 with the solution for crRNA λ4.2:tracr RNA.
Add 1 μL of milliQ H2O to complete the crRNA λ4.2:tracr RNA mix preparation.
Mix 2 μL of 5 μM crRNA λ4.1 with the appropriate volume of reagents as specified.
Pipette 1 μL of 10 μM tracr RNA into the mixture.
Add 4 μL of 1× T50 buffer to the mixture.
Add 1 μL of milliQ H2O to complete the crRNA λ4.1:tracr RNA mix.
Heat the crRNA λ4.1:tracr RNA mix at 95°C for 2 minutes.
Cool down the heated mixture to 25°C.
Repeat steps involving mixing, pipetting, and heating for crRNA λ4.02:tracr RNA mix as described.
Dilute Alt-R S.p. D10A nickase to a final concentration of 5 μM in PBS (ratio of enzyme to buffer is 0.8 μL to 9.2 μL).
Add 2 μL of the diluted enzyme to each crRNA:tracr RNA mix.
Incubate the mixture at 25°C for 5 minutes.
Mix 175 μL of λ DNA with 20 μL of 10×Cas9 digestion buffer, and add 2 μL each of Cas9 D10A-crRNA λ2-tracr RNA complex and Cas9 D10A-crRNA λ5-tracr RNA complex for generating λ2/5 gDNA precursor.
Incubate the mixture at 37°C for 1 hour to complete digestion.
Mix 175 μL of λ DNA with 20 μL of 10×Cas9 digestion buffer, and add 2 μL each of Cas9 D10A-crRNA λ4-tracr RNA complex and Cas9 D10A-crRNA λ5-tracr RNA complex for generating λ4/5 gDNA precursor.
Incubate the mixture at 37°C for 1 hour to complete digestion.
Mix 175 μL of λ DNA with 20 μL of 10×Cas9 digestion buffer, and add 2 μL each of Cas9 D10A-crRNA λ4.2-tracr RNA complex and Cas9 D10A-crRNA λ4-tracr RNA complex for generating λ4.2/4 gDNA precursor.
Incubate the mixture at 37°C for 1 hour to complete digestion.
Add 175 μL of λ DNA from Step 2e, 20 μL 10×Cas9 digestion buffer, 2 μL of 10 nM Cas9 D10A-crRNA λ4.1-tracr RNA complex, and 2 μL of 10 nM Cas9 D10A-crRNA λ4-tracr RNA complex.
Incubate at 37°C for 1 h.
Add 500 mM EDTA (pH 8.0) to a final concentration of 10 mM to terminate the reaction.
Store the reaction at 4°C.
Avoid pipetting up-and-down during the procedure.
Cut the ends of pipette tips carefully.
Do not purify nicked constructs at the final stage.
Store λ gDNA precursors at 4°C for 3–4 weeks.
Flush channels with 0.5 mL of 5% bleach solution at 1.5 bar.
Flush channels with 1.0 mL of milliQ H2O at 1.5 bar.
Flush channels with 0.5 mL of 10 mM sodium thiosulfate at 1.5 bar.
Flush channels with 0.5 mL of filtered sterile PBS at 1.5 bar.
Flush channels with 0.5 mL of 0.5% Pluronics F127 (w/v) in filtered sterile PBS at 1.5 bar.
Flush channels with 0.5 mL of 0.1% BSA (w/v) in filtered sterile PBS at 1.5 bar.
Add water on the objective.
Raise the objective to touch the microfluidics chip.
Start trapping laser at 0.31 pN/nm trap stiffness (for 4.5-μm beads).
Find appropriate z position for the trapping laser in the middle of the microfluidics channel.
Add oil on top of the microfluidics chip.
Lower the condenser to close position, where reflection image is fully visible on the camera.
Inspect the reflection image to ensure absence of bubbles in immersion oil and proper condenser position.
Lower laser power of the trapping laser to reach 0.14 pN/nm trap stiffness.
Add 4.5-μm SPHERO Streptavidin Coated polystyrene particles in filtered sterile PBS at 0.005% w/v to channel 1.
Add 0.2% (v/v) λ gDNA precursor constructs prepared in Step 4 of the protocol in filtered sterile PBS to channel 2.
Add filtered sterile PBS to channel 3.
Add 5 nM RPA-eGFP in buffer 0.5×NTM supplemented with 0.2 mg/mL BSA and the oxygen scavenger system with 5 mM protocatechuic acid (PCA), 100 nM protocatechuic dioxygenase (PCD) to channel 4.
Add 50 nM SYTOX Orange in filtered sterile PBS to channel 5.
Flow enough liquid through the system to observe beads in channel 1 in brightfield.
Capture a pair of beads in channel 1 and move to channel 2.
Perform force calibration according to manufacturer instruction at 0.14 pN/nm trap stiffness.
Move beads apart to a sufficient distance (we suggest 25 μm between the bead edges).
Adjust z position in Trap XY settings to get both beads into the focus.
Turn on single-photon counter module.
Turn on blue laser to 5% laser power.
Turn on green laser to 10% laser power.
Set pixel size to 100 nm.
Perform a single 2D scan and adjust scanning area to include both beads.
Ensure reflection in the middle of the beads in the blue channel is sharp and bright.
Trap two evenly shaped (bead match score > 0.97) streptavidin-coated beads in channel 1.
Move traps to channel 2.
Set “ping-pong” option that automatically moves the traps between 5 μm ('close') and 17 μm ('extended') distance marks at 6.0 μm/s speed with 1–2 s dwell time at 5 μm position.
Set force to zero at 5 μm 'close' distance between the bead edges.
Keep pressure of 0.12–0.18 bar to maintain buffer flow.
Monitor force-extension curve using built-in worm-like chain models.
Set an example curve for a single λ dsDNA molecule.
Turn off the buffer flow if a single molecule of λ gDNA precursor is captured.
Close all channels once capture is confirmed.
Move the traps to channel 3 after closing the channels.
Repeat the process by picking up new beads from channel 1 if multiple DNA molecules are captured simultaneously.
Extend the bead distance beyond 23 μm to break one or more extra molecules captured between the beads.
Move the beads to 'close’ distance in channel 3.
Set force to zero.
Slowly extend the DNA molecule to a distance between 23–25 μm (or 65 pN force) for short gaps or 27–29 μm (or 100 pN force) for longer gaps.
Hold λ gDNA precursor at high force for 30 – 60 seconds.
Move the beads to a distance of 5 to 10 μm.
Wait for 1 minute at low force.
Slowly re-extend captured construct to 15 pN force.
Monitor the force-extension curve.
Repeat the process one more time to ensure complete gap melting.
Compare recorded force-extension curves to worm-like chain model of λ dsDNA with contour length corresponding to individual λ gDNA constructs.
Move the traps to channel 4.
Bring in the beads to ‘close’ position.
Set force to zero.
Activate force clamp and set the value to 5 pN or 15 pN.
Turn off the force clamp.
Take 2D image of λ gDNA and beads.
Stain for dsDNA content by moving the beads to channel 5 containing SYTOX Orange.
Take another 2D scan.
Wash the flow cell as described in the previous section.
Align the microscope as described in the previous section.
Add 4.5-μm SPHERO Streptavidin coated polystyrene particles in filtered sterile PBS at 0.005% w/v to channel 1.
Add 0.2% (v/v) λ2/5 gDNA precursor construct prepared previously in filtered sterile PBS to channel 2.
Supplement buffer 0.5×NTM with components as described and add it to the channels.
Mix 0.2 mg/mL BSA with buffer 1×NTM (50 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.5, 100 mM NaCl, 1.0 mM MgCl2) supplemented with 1 mM ATP and the ATP regeneration system.
Add the oxygen scavenger system containing 5 mM PCA and 100 nM PCD to channel 3.
Mix 500 nM RAD-51 with buffer 1×NTM (50 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.5, 100 mM NaCl, 1.0 mM MgCl2) supplemented with 0.2 mg/mL BSA, 1 mM ATP, and the oxygen scavenger system containing 5 mM PCA and 100 nM PCD.
Add the mixture to channel 4.
Perform force calibration.
Set up confocal imaging.
Capture beads and tether a single piece of λ gDNA precursor as described previously.
Move the traps to channel 3.
Move the beads to ‘close’ distance.
Set force to zero.
Slowly extend the DNA molecule to 27–29 μm distance or 100 pN force to generate longer gaps.
Hold λ gDNA precursor at high force for 30 – 60 seconds.
Move the beads to 5 to 10 μm distance.
Wait for 1–5 minutes for DNA strands to re-anneal as RPA-eGFP slows it down.
Slowly re-extend captured construct to 15 pN force.
Monitor force-extension curve.
Compare recorded force-extension curve to worm-like chain model of λ2/5 gDNA construct.
Take a 2D image of your λ2/5 gDNA and beads.
Verify the presence of RPA-eGFP signal covering expected length of λ gDNA at the expected genomic position.
Ensure no additional nicks or gaps are present in the DNA.
Keep λ gDNA to length corresponding to 15 pN force.
Set up kymograph imaging mode by scanning a single line of pixels through the center of trapped beads and DNA.
Set line-time to 5 seconds.
Start imaging immediately.
Move traps to channel 4.
Continue building kymograph of RPA-eGFP displacement.
Monitor force simultaneously with fluorescence measurement.
Observe RAD-51 displacement as loss of blue fluorescence signal.
Expect minimal loss of RPA-eGFP signal in the absence of RAD-51 for at least 20 minutes.
Prepare a fresh batch of PCA/PCD if rapid fluorescence loss is observed due to photobleaching.

Find an optimal concentration of RAD-51 where fast-enough assembly can be observed by adding increasing concentrations of RAD-51 to channel 4 (e.g., from 200 to 2000 nM protein) and performing a few assembly experiments for each concentration.
Passivate the channel with 1 ml of 0.5% BSA in PBS if inefficient filament assembly is observed on the first DNA molecules captured.
Repeat assembly experiments after passivating the channel.
Include 10 nM free RPA-eGFP with RAD-51 in channel 4 to better resolve individual growing RAD-51 filaments, which will suppress RAD-51 nucleation on ssDNA.
